title: I made a free Blender add-on that turns a prompt into a textured, rigged character, with local models (and showcased it in Unreal)
author: sakalond
selftext:
StableGen is my free, open-source Blender add-on. It runs local models through ComfyUI, so nothing goes to a paid API:

* Prompt -> a few candidate images -> a TRELLIS.2 mesh.
* Texturing: every camera view is generated (Qwen Image 2.1 here) and projected onto the mesh, with PBR maps.
* Masked Edit: paint a part of the model and describe the change, for example swapping the jacket for armor, without redoing the rest.
* Auto-rig with SkinTokens, then retarget walks or runs (the walk in the video is from Mixamo).
* Export as GLB/FBX: the village in the video is 12 props made the same way and dropped into Unreal Engine 5.7.

Current limits: the meshes are dense triangles, so for production you'd retopologize or decimate and bake (this is possible within the plugin). Texture quality depends a lot on the prompt and the model you pick. Qwen Image 2.1 is non-commercial; the add-on also supports models you can use commercially, such as SDXL and MOSS Image.

GitHub: [https://github.com/sakalond/StableGen](https://github.com/sakalond/StableGen)  
Guide: [https://github.com/sakalond/StableGen/wiki](https://github.com/sakalond/StableGen/wiki)

comments.body:
Download: [https://github.com/sakalond/StableGen/releases/latest](https://github.com/sakalond/StableGen/releases/latest) (one ZIP per platform, with an installer for ComfyUI and the models).



Ran on an RTX 4080 (16 GB). Happy to answer questions about the pipeline, or join the Discord: [https://discord.gg/jhGp9Rsgh3](https://discord.gg/jhGp9Rsgh3)

replies.author: NoBatsHere
replies.body:
I'll check it out later. But how would you say this is better than a pipeline that Claude would have naturally built on its own with many rounds of AI feedback and a few rounds of human feedback?

How does it handle complex creature like a crab? 
How does it handle made up creatures with no clear reference?
How does it handle unique objects with unique animations?

I've got a pretty comprehensive suite for gamedev built at this point that runs as a webapp and does everything. But I have not done a dedicated deep dive into refining my creature animation workflow yet.

So what are the unique strengths you brought to this and how is it better than what Claude would do on its own?

All that aside, great work and it will be helpful for some no matter what.

replies.author: sakalond
replies.body:
I think it can serve as a good tool for Claude with Blender MCP. I already use it like that. But it's also built for manual workflows. 

Obviously the landscape shifted since I started working on this project, and much of the functionality could now be reproduced with agentic workflows. It's still pretty complex and has has a lot of modes, parameters and logic behind it, and has been through a lot of testing to make it work well, which I don't think would be that quick to replicate if it didn't already exist. It will also save you tokens and time to use this instead of implementing from scratch.
